rec.source_name: Erich Friedman, Packing Center: Circles in Circles
rec.citation: r = 3.304+ Proved by Braaksma in 1963.
rec.conversion_note: The source's disks have radius 1 in a container of radius r; this site's disks have diameter 1 and a circle is scored by its diameter, so the same packing at half the scale has container diameter r: the value is unchanged. The source prints a truncated decimal (marked +), stored as printed. More digits (3.304764870962) from Eckard Specht, Packomania: The best known packings of equal circles in a circle, http://www.packomania.com/cci/: The source fixes the container (radius 1) and lists the circle radius. This site fixes the circle diameter at 1, so the container diameter is 1 / radius, the source's "ratio" column. Coordinates are the source's, divided by the circle diameter (twice the radius).
rec.coordinates_note: Coordinates from Eckard Specht, Packomania: The best known packings of equal circles in a circle, http://www.packomania.com/cci/ (read 2026-10-07).
